meta.title: CZ-6A Launch visibility
notes: Reconstruction (revision 5, 2026-11-28), not telemetry or a unique solution. Liftoff was announced at 18:15 Beijing time (10:15 UTC). The model uses 10:15:08 UTC: the second is fitted, with a broad minimum at 7 to 10 s, and agrees with the 8.5 s by which the catalog orbits of Yaogan-50 03 and 04 differ in phase relative to their announced minutes.

The vehicle is a point-mass CZ-6A with published masses and thrusts, the typical flight sequence (booster burnout 114.5 s, separation 117.5 s, fairing 179 s, stage separation 238.5 s; stage-2 ignition at 240 s is assumed) and explicit drag. Its thrust direction follows one smooth law: vertical rise, pitch-over and gravity turn to T+90 s, then the tangent of the thrust elevation falls linearly in time to cutoff, continuous through staging (50° at T+90 s, 38° at stage separation, −4° at cutoff). Revision 3 had pitch nodes at the staging times and steps of up to 38° at ignition.

Stage 2 has the propulsion of Yaogan-50 04, the same vehicle on the same corridor, whose cutoff was observed: a 585 s burn to T+825 s at an assumed 176.5 kN, from 38.9 t to 8.0 t. This flight was not observed at cutoff. The cutoff state is fitted to the first catalog elements of 2026-240A (assumed payload; identity unconfirmed) and lies 0.03 km from that SGP4 state. Revisions 2 to 4 assumed a 533 s burn to T+773.4 s.

The two untimed ground reports of this flight carry little weight, because their measurement error is unknown: at N39.00 E110.12 the rocket crossed above the Moon at 1.6x its elevation (model 1.72x), and at N37.76 E110.93 the sunlit rising path looked nearly straight.

With that stage 2 the fitted thrust scale is 0.984, against 1.06 from the December 2025 calibration and 0.987 from the separate Yaogan-50 04 fit, and the boosters fall 349 km from the pad, at the centre of their zone. With the earlier 533 s burn the thrust scale was 0.927 and the boosters fell 69 km short.

The plane change starts in stage 1: the thrust stays in the launch plane (azimuth 255.07°) until booster separation, so that the boosters fall into the zone of NOTAM A5283/26, then yaws out of it (3.6° by core cutoff) and continues smoothly through stage 2. How the turn is shared between the stages follows from that assumed law. Staging times follow the typical published CZ-6A sequence, not this flight’s telemetry, and are not shown as timeline events.
NOTAM 10:07–10:28 UTC is a hazard-area activation interval, not launch-time limits or an insertion constraint. The 09:30–11:00 UTC selector is an exploratory range, not an announced launch window.
Shifting T0 reuses the same Earth-fixed (ECEF) trajectory and changes the solar geometry; it does not reoptimize dynamics or propagate a newly fitted orbit.

Source positions and velocities use a TEME-like frame with GMST rotation, UTC approximating UT1 and no polar motion. The exporter converts to ECEF and resamples with cubic Hermite interpolation; it does not reoptimize or integrate a new trajectory.
The upper-stage and orbit dynamics include central gravity and J2. Higher harmonics, post-insertion maneuvers, fragmentation and debris descent are not modeled.
Altitude samples are WGS84 geodetic ellipsoidal heights in km. Perigee and apogee are orbital radii minus the WGS84 equatorial radius; these are not the same altitude convention.

Sunlight pickup is the first moment the refracted Sun-centre ray clears the WGS84 ellipsoid: standard atmosphere, 1.10° of bending for a ray that grazes the surface. Here that is T+96.3 s (10:16:44.3 UTC) at 33.3 km; the straight ray gives T+108.4 s at 44.2 km. The Sun is from the shared DE440s ephemeris, linearly interpolated in ECEF at 30-second cadence.

The 10° visibility envelope is sampled during sunlit ascent for sea-level observers with Sun-centre altitude ≤0°, then clipped to the observer night side at the insertion reference epoch. Post-insertion orbit tracks do not enlarge the ascent envelope.

The first sunlight is weak and red: about 0.1% of full Sun 8 s after pickup, 1% after 13 s and 10% after 27 s, turning orange, cream, pale blue (ozone) and white. The page models none of that, nor weather, terrain, finite solar-disc emergence or plume size. Geometric visibility is not a claim of naked-eye detection.
The 1.5 revolutions shown are exactly 1.5 times the insertion Keplerian period in elapsed time, not a claim of an exact J2 ground-track repeat or true-anomaly recurrence.

The model TLE keeps the label PRELAUNCH MODEL - NOT OBSERVED and placeholder catalog number 00000. It is fitted to the reconstructed numerical orbit and is not the catalog element set; some TLE consumers reject this placeholder.

The rocket drawing follows that sequence: the four solid boosters burn to T+114.5 s and drop at T+117.5 s, the fairing at T+179 s and stage 1 at T+238.5 s; stage 2 ignites at T+240 s, and from insertion only the payload is drawn. These are drawing states, not timeline events.
about: Reconstruction with a calibrated CZ-6A vehicle model, one smooth steering law and the first catalog orbit; not telemetry.
